effect: The turning sensors are built; fluid movement bends their hairs and changes a nerve signal.

reason: The mineral weights sit on the jelly layer above the tilt sensor cells, matching the second goal.
expectation: The weights and sensor cells should form the weighted tilt sensors.

reaction: The two kinds of sensors now have clearer, different jobs.
reason: The balance nerves are pictured connecting both kinds of sensor to the brain, so I will start with the turning sensors.
expectation: The turning sensors should connect to a nerve route toward the brain.

reaction: I expected the nerve connection first, so the required order surprised me.
reason: The balance nerves are shown leading from both kinds of sensor to the brain.
expectation: The balance organs should connect to nerves leading toward the brain.

effect: The balance organs now have nerve routes to the brain; they still need connecting to the body's movements.
reaction: The nerve connection worked as expected.
reason: The eye and posture nerve routes lead from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles that help keep the body steady.
expectation: The balance signals should connect to routes controlling eye and posture muscles.

alternatives.reason: The balance organs also need to connect to the existing body.

effect: The balance sensors now connect through the brain and spinal cord to eye and posture muscles.
reaction: The route from the sensors to movement is clearer now.
reason: The connected sensors still need to be brought into the existing body model.
expectation: The body should gain the balance sensors and their movement connections.

effect: The completed body model shows how balance signals help stabilize the eyes and adjust posture, alongside vision and signals from muscles and joints.
reaction: The eyes turning opposite to the head was a clear and satisfying result.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the two sensor types was most worthwhile: the pictures showed how turning and tilting shift different materials to bend sensory hairs.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the parts in separate stages felt a little repetitive, though it made the route to the muscles clear.

surprise.text: I expected to connect the turning sensors to nerves first, but the game joined the two sensor types before allowing that connection.

arbitrary.text: Joining the two sensor types before attaching nerves felt like a game prerequisite; the pictures showed both connecting to nerves but did not explain why they had to be joined first.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter because the final picture connected the inner-ear parts to a familiar action: keeping your eyes on something while turning your head.
